module purpose: Implements a JTAG TAP + Debug Transport Module: it synchronizes JTAG inputs, runs the TAP state machine and IR/DR access (IDCODE, DTMCS, DMI), controls a DMI controller that latches requests and drives dmi_req_o, and consumes DMI responses on dmi_rsp_i.

use-case flows.value: Start a DMI transaction: capture op/addr/wdata from the JTAG DMI register into dmi_ctrl and set busy to begin the transaction
Issue the DMI request to the external DMI consumer by driving dmi_req_o.op / dmi_req_o.data / dmi_req_o.addr from the dmi_ctrl registers
Handle DMI response: capture dmi_rsp_i.data into dmi_ctrl.rdata and clear busy when ack is observed
Write/read TAP DR registers (IDCODE, DTMCS, DMI): DR_CAPTURE loads readback values into tap_reg.*, DR_SHIFT shifts TDI into the selected DR field(s)
Shift out selected register bits to JTAG TDO (idcode, dtmcs, dmi, or bypass) on tck_falling, selected by tap_reg.ireg and the TAP state
DTMCS-derived resets (dmireset, dmihardreset) are transferred into the DMI controller and clear error state when asserted
dmi_ctrl.busy acts as a lock that prevents new DMI requests from being started while a transaction is in flight

conceptual assets.concept: DMI request message (op, addr, wdata) sent to the external DMI consumer
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module latches request fields into the DMI controller registers and drives them onto the external interface: dmi_ctrl.op/wdata/addr are set from the selected JTAG DMI register when a DR_UPDATE trigger and selection occur (lines 263-271 and 266-271), and the outputs dmi_req_o.op/data/addr are driven from those registers (lines 283-285). The RTL therefore establishes an integrity objective: the external DMI consumer must receive exactly the op/address/data this module computes. The map shows the port fields copy from the controller registers (port dmi_req_o.* COPIES dmi_ctrl.* at the occurrences cited below) and the controller registers are clocked storage for the request (CLOCKED_BY clk_i).

conceptual assets.concept: DMI controller busy flag that serializes transactions (exclusive lock)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The dmi_ctrl.busy register is used to prevent new request formation and to gate controller behaviour: when busy='0' the controller may latch a new op/addr/wdata and set busy to '1' (lines 264-271); when a response ack arrives busy is cleared (lines 274-277). The RTL therefore establishes that the busy bit's correctness is required to preserve correct request sequencing and avoid overlapping transactions. The map shows busy is stored (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) and is used as a gate in the controller records.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI reset controls that force DMI reset state and clear errors (dmireset, dmihardreset sourced from DTMCS)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The DTMCS bits (dtmcs) determine dmi_ctrl.dmireset and dmi_ctrl.dmihardreset when a DR_UPDATE of the DTMCS register is observed (dmi_controller lines 247-251). The controller also uses these reset flags to clear err (line 256) and to inhibit request start (lines 264-271). Thus the integrity of the reset-control bits (and of the DTMCS field that supplies them) is established by the RTL as needed for correct reset and error behaviour. The map shows dmi_ctrl.dmireset/dmihardreset are registers (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) and that tap_reg.dtmcs is the captured register backing those fields (CLOCKED_BY and copied from dtmcs_nxt).

conceptual assets.concept: DMI register contents (tap_reg.dmi) provided by JTAG and consumed to form DMI transactions
conceptual assets.reasoning: The JTAG-accessible DMI DR (tap_reg.dmi) is the point where the requester writes op/addr/data (via DR_SHIFT / DR_CAPTURE) and the controller later samples those fields to build a DMI request (lines 189 and 266-271). The RTL therefore establishes that the contents of the DMI register are the source of DMI requests and their integrity matters. The map shows tap_reg.dmi is a clocked register (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) that is copied from tap_reg.dmi_nxt on DR_CAPTURE and whose fields are sourced into dmi_ctrl.addr/wdata/op (map records and the cited lines).

conceptual assets.concept: DR-update trigger (dr_trigger.valid) that enables register updates and DMI starts
conceptual assets.reasoning: A two-stage shift register produces dr_trigger.valid when a DR_UPDATE event occurs (update_trigger process lines 146-156 and concurrent assignment line 161). The DMI controller and DTMCS update logic only act when dr_trigger.valid = '1' (lines 247, 258, 265), so the correct value of dr_trigger.valid is required for enabling or preventing updates and DMI starts. The map records show dr_trigger.valid is computed from dr_trigger.sreg (GATED_BY at the cited occurrence) and is used as a gate in dmi_controller.

conceptual assets.concept: TAP controller state (tap_ctrl_state) that selects IR/DR behaviour and gates register operations
conceptual assets.reasoning: The tap_control process implements the TAP state machine (lines 116-141). Many register accesses and TDO behaviour are gated by tap_ctrl_state (reg_access uses it to choose IR vs DR actions at lines 178-196 and the TDO assignments at lines 202-211), so the correctness of tap_ctrl_state is required for correct IR/DR sequencing and access semantics. The map shows tap_ctrl_state is a clocked register (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) and is used in SELECTED_BY/GATED_BY records where those decisions occur.

conceptual assets.concept: IR register (tap_reg.ireg) selecting which DR is accessed and which data is shifted out
conceptual assets.reasoning: The IR register is loaded and shifted in reg_access (lines 178-181) and it selects which DR (IDCODE/DTMCS/DMI/bypass) is captured, shifted, and presented on TDO (lines 185-196 and 202-211). The RTL therefore establishes the IR value as critical to selecting which debug register is accessed; its integrity directly affects which data is exposed or modified. The map shows tap_reg.ireg is a clocked register (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) and appears in the SELECTED_BY records that route DR operations.

conceptual assets.concept: JTAG TDO output stream (jtag_tdo_o) that reports register bits externally
conceptual assets.reasoning: On the falling edge of synchronized TCK the module drives jtag_tdo_o from the selected register bit (IR shift path or the current DR selected bit) so correctness of the bitstream presented on TDO is required for correct JTAG readback and capture semantics (lines 202-211). The map shows jtag_tdo_o is driven from internal registers (DERIVES_FROM / COPIES records at the cited occurrences) and gated by TAP state and tck_falling, establishing the relationship.

conceptual assets.concept: IDCODE register value used for device identification readback
conceptual assets.reasoning: When the IDCODE DR is captured the module loads IDCODE_VERSION/IDCODE_PARTID/IDCODE_MANID into tap_reg.idcode (line 187) and then shifts it out via TDO if selected (lines 194 and 207). The RTL therefore establishes integrity of the IDCODE readback. The map shows tap_reg.idcode is a clocked register (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) with a constant capture driver (the IDCODE generics) and selected TDO sourcing as shown in the cited records.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI response data as received from the external DMI (dmi_rsp_i.data) and stored for JTAG readback (dmi_ctrl.rdata)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Responses from the external DMI interface are consumed at dmi_rsp_i.data and copied into the controller rdata register (line 274) so that read results can be presented back via the DMI register and JTAG. The RTL therefore establishes that the correctness of incoming response data and of the stored rdata value matters for correct read-return behaviour. The map records show dmi_rsp_i.data CARRIES into dmi_ctrl.rdata at the cited occurrence and that dmi_ctrl.rdata is stored by CLOCKED_BY clk_i.
